title: Na+‐dependent transport of taurine is found only on the abluminal membrane of the blood‐brain barrier

sections.abstract: <jats:p> Luminal and abluminal plasma membranes, isolated from bovine brain microvessels, were used to characterize Na <jats:sup>+</jats:sup> ‐dependent and facilitative taurine transport. Initial transmembrane potential was − 59 mV 0, external Na <jats:sup>+</jats:sup> was 126 mM, and T= 25°C. Apparent affinity constants of the taurine transporters were determined over a range of taurine concentrations from 0.24 μM to 11.4 μM. Abluminal membranes had Na <jats:sup>+</jats:sup> ‐dependent taurine transport as well as facilitative transport; luminal membranes only had facilitative transport. Apparent K <jats:sub>m</jats:sub> 's for facilitative and Na <jats:sup>+</jats:sup> ‐dependent taurine transports were 0.06 ± 0.02 μM and 0.7 ± 0.1 μM, respectively. Na <jats:sup>+</jats:sup> ‐dependent transport of taurine was voltage dependent between −25 to −101 mV. Transport was over 5 times greater at −101 mV compared with V <jats:sub>m</jats:sub> was −25 mV. Sensitivity to external osmolality of Na <jats:sup>+</jats:sup> ‐dependent transport was studied over a range of osmolalities (229 to 398 mOsm/kg H <jats:sub>2</jats:sub> O) using mannitol as the osmotic agent to adjust osmolality. For these experiments the concentration of Na <jats:sup>+</jats:sup> wasmaintained constant at 50 mM; the calculated transmembrane potential was −59 mV. Na <jats:sup>+</jats:sup> ‐dependent transport was sensitive to osmolality with the greatest rate observed at 229 mOsm/kg H <jats:sub>2</jats:sub> O. </jats:p>
